entries.test: Post-IPO financial statements and financing disclosures would show whether each company requires at least $50 billion in annual debt funding.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion frames the need as post-IPO and applies it to each company, not their combined borrowing. The debt requirement is firm; the rating prediction is only likely.

entries.test: CoreWeave's financing disclosures through 2030 would show whether it continues borrowing on its own credit rather than exclusively against counterparties' credit.
entries.note: The funding estimate is attributed to UBS; the conclusion about independent borrowing is Zitron's.

entries.test: Debt pricing, credit spreads, lender commentary and project disclosures would show whether power delays, local opposition and repayment concerns are increasing data center borrowing costs.
entries.note: The possible nonpayment describes investors' concerns, not a probabilistic hedge on the asserted pricing effect.

entries.test: Changes in AI data center debt yields, benchmark Treasury yields and credit spreads would establish whether both benchmark rates and sector risk premiums have increased borrowing costs.

entries.note: The extracted claim judges forecasts as stupid and wasteful; it does not endorse the $32 trillion forecast.

entries.test: After an Anthropic IPO and an announced annual fundraising target of at least roughly $47.5 billion, financing disclosures and historical junk issuance rankings would test the predicted funding constraints and issuance scale.

entries.note: He says funding operations likely precludes asset-backed structures. The customer-payment exception is explicit in the next paragraph.

entries.test: Published credit ratings and rationales would show whether either company obtains investment-grade debt at the cited EBITDA profile without government or hyperscaler guarantees.
entries.note: “At that EBITDA” refers to the severe financial profile just quantified, rather than negative EBITDA generally. Investment-grade exclusion is firm, while the B-to-CCC+ band is hedged.
Calling the rating an unprecedented regulatory failure is an evaluative judgment.

entries.test: Under the stated valuation and funding assumptions, annual debt issuance and associated credit ratings would show whether either company raises $50 billion without the exceptional rating described.
entries.note: The financing limit is a factual claim despite the accompanying criticism of ratings agencies.
“If I had to guess” and “maybe” explicitly make this tentative.
The extracted proposition principally recommends abandoning these comparisons.

entries.test: The deal's contractual requirements, both companies' financial resources and Oracle's available compute capacity would test the claimed inability to finance and serve it.
entries.note: This extracts the asserted financial and capacity constraints without the separate claim about media and market attitudes.
The main clause describes apparent current borrowing; Anthropic's future survival is explicitly left as a possibility either way.

entries.test: If Anthropic reaches $100 billion in annual operating expenses, its cash generation and debt financing compared with historical corporate cash flows and the CCC market would test the stated alternatives.
entries.note: The debt-market alternative appears in the full sentence even though the supplied exact-words excerpt omits it.

entries.test: Publicly documented AI compute purchases by customers other than OpenAI and Anthropic would test the asserted $22 billion ceiling on identifiable purchases.
entries.note: This is presented as the limit of his search, rather than an audited total. The surrounding discussion concerns current AI compute demand.
Both the open-source outcome and the Google alternative are explicitly probabilistic.

entries.test: Disclosed non-cancellable commitments and operating cost breakdowns would show whether those obligations prevent either company from reducing its costs.
entries.note: The categorical wording is stronger than merely saying cost reductions would be difficult.

entries.test: Comparable AI-company growth rates, customer counts and customer-composition disclosures would test both the claimed competitive gap and the predominance of AI startups among customers.
If the described debt defaults, lab payment failures and GPU-sales collapse occur, subsequent hyperscaler earnings against prior forecasts and NVIDIA revenue would test the predicted losses.
entries.note: The 90% figure is an upper extent, not a prediction of an exact 90% decline.

entries.test: In the described collapse over the next few years, neocloud financial statements, defaults, investor recoveries and GPU resale inventories would test the predicted cash exhaustion, losses and supply glut.
entries.note: The conditional scenario carries over from the preceding sentence. “The next few years” places the horizon beyond the evaluation date.

entries.test: NVIDIA revenue growth, customer capital spending and the debt financing supporting that spending would test the asserted dependence of sustained growth on continuing debt issuance.
entries.note: Customer survival is hedged, but the asserted financing dependency is firm.

entries.test: Hyperscaler investor presentations, comparative Fortune 500 balance sheets and GPU resale values outside AI booms would test the asserted lack of alternative growth businesses, asset burden and GPU value dependence.
entries.note: “Ideas to sell investors” concerns publicly presented growth prospects, rather than undisclosed private ideas.
“The most glaring miss in the history of finance” is rhetorical emphasis without a shared factual ranking.
